regulatory_history.title: FTC v. Kochava Inc. and Collective Data Solutions, LLC (D. Idaho No. 2:22-cv-00377): stipulated order
regulatory_history.body: US District Court for the District of Idaho, in a case brought by the US Federal Trade Commission
regulatory_history.notes: Filed 2022-08-29. The first complaint was dismissed with leave to amend (2023-05-04); motions to dismiss the amended complaints were denied (2024-02-03, 2025-02-03). The order bars selling or sharing location data tied to sensitive places in the US and runs 10 years. Collective Data Solutions, which took over part of the data business in 2023, is bound too. Kochava's own 2022 suit against the FTC was dismissed on 2023-05-03.

regulatory_history.title: Murphy v. Kochava, Inc. (D. Idaho No. 2:23-cv-00058): class settlement approved
regulatory_history.body: US District Court for the District of Idaho
regulatory_history.notes: Consolidated suits filed in 2022 and 2023, including Maattala's from Massachusetts. Injunctive relief only: a privacy block for sensitive locations, SDK data limited to the app that collected it, deletion of older SDK data kept for Kochava's own benefit, an opt-out list, and consent checks on data suppliers. Class members keep their right to seek damages.

sources.title: Murphy v. Kochava, Inc. (D. Idaho No. 2:23-cv-00058), final order approving the class settlement
sources.quote: restrictions limiting any SDK-collected data to use by the originating app developer; and permanent deletion of legacy SDK data retained for Kochava’s own benefit

sources.title: Murphy v. Kochava, Inc. (D. Idaho No. 2:23-cv-00058), final order approving the class settlement
sources.quote: a “privacy block” that filters and prevents dissemination of location data associated with Sensitive Locations

sources.title: Murphy v. Kochava, Inc. (D. Idaho No. 2:23-cv-00058), final order approving the class settlement
sources.quote: a consumer opt-out and … blacklisting mechanism to prevent future ingestion or sale of covered data

sources.title: Murphy v. Kochava, Inc. (D. Idaho No. 2:23-cv-00058), final order approving the class settlement
sources.quote: a verification process requiring Kochava to obtain representative consent prompts from data suppliers

sources.title: Murphy v. Kochava, Inc. (D. Idaho No. 2:23-cv-00058), final order approving the class settlement

regulatory_history.title: Greenley v. Kochava, Inc. (S.D. Cal. No. 3:22-cv-01327)
regulatory_history.body: US District Court for the Southern District of California
regulatory_history.notes: Alleged that Kochava's SDK secretly collected app users' data, which Kochava sold for advertising (not proven in court). The court let part of the case go ahead on 2023-07-27; it was dismissed without prejudice by agreement on 2024-10-17.

sources.title: Greenley v. Kochava, Inc. (S.D. Cal. No. 3:22-cv-01327), order on the motion to dismiss
sources.quote: Defendant coded its SDK for data collection and embedded it in third-party apps; the SDK secretly collected app users’ data

sources.title: Greenley v. Kochava, Inc. (S.D. Cal. No. 3:22-cv-01327), order on the motion to dismiss
